title: Pauri 23, sound: saalaahee saalaah
hook: saalaahee saalaah etee surat na paaeeaa
tomorrow: Pauri 23, meaning: the ant who remembers

segments.voice: Yesterday, worlds beyond worlds. Your line was the writing runs out. Did you stop a growing list, once, and look up? Today, the ones who praise. Day one hundred ninety-nine.

A superfan of a band can recite every lyric and every tour. They've been to the shows, bought the records, worn the shirts. They praise and praise. Ask why the music moves them, though, and the answer often trails off into a shrug and a smile. The love is real; the explanation runs out. Praising something and fully grasping it aren't the same. Pauri 23 opens with the people who praise, and a gentle, honest line about what they still don't know.
screen: `A SUPERFAN.` → `THEY PRAISE AND PRAISE.` → `PRAISING ISN'T GRASPING.`

segments.voice: Here's the first line of Pauri 23 in the original: saalaahee saalaah etee surat na paaeeaa. Let's take it slowly. Saalaah, saa-LAAH: praise. We met it in Pauri 19: akharee saalaah, through letters, praise. Saalaahee, saa-laa-HEE: the praisers, those who praise. So saalaahee saalaah: the praisers praise. The same root twice, like an echo. Etee: this much, so much. Surat: awareness, understanding. You know that word; it was our word on day one hundred eighty-four, the waking attention that trust brings. Na paaeeaa: have not obtained, have not reached. Put together: the praisers praise, but have not reached an understanding of how great. Hear the music of it. Saalaahee saalaah, soft and flowing, the long aa sounds like breath going out. Then etee surat na paaeeaa, the line tips over, as if it's shrugging. Notice the tone. This isn't criticism of the people who praise. Japji is full of praise. It's the same honesty that runs all through these stanzas: no pen for this, the writing runs out, only the Maker knows. Even the ones who praise the most haven't grasped the size of it. And that's not a failure. Praise doesn't need a complete understanding to be real. The rest of the stanza, tomorrow, gives a picture of that: rivers, the sea, and a very small ant. Today, the sound. Saalaahee saalaah.
screen: `SAALAAH — PRAISE.` · `SAALAAHEE — THE ONES WHO PRAISE.` · `SURAT — AWARENESS, AGAIN.` · `PRAISE WITHOUT FULL GRASP.` · then, large: `SAALAAHEE.`

segments.voice: Say the first line aloud: saalaahee saalaah, etee surat na paaeeaa. Once slowly, letting the long aa sounds breathe out. Twice more, softer each time. Then sit, and listen to the quiet after the last aa fades. Let the line keep echoing, without working out what it means. That's tomorrow's job. The bell holds the time.
Pauri 23. It opens saalaahee saalaah, etee surat na paaeeaa: the praisers praise, but haven't grasped how great.
Your line: saalaahee. Today, when you admire something, a song, a view, someone's skill, let the admiring be enough, without needing to explain it. Day one hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: Pauri 23 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; praise, saalaah, is at the center of Sikh worship, sung as kirtan in gurdwaras every day.

original.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 23, line 1: the praisers praise, but have not reached an understanding of how great.

trapdoor: what you thought: people who praise God understand God.
what it means: praise is real, but even the greatest praisers haven't grasped how great.
what a scholar hears: saalaahee and saalaah share one root, like an echo; surat, awareness, returns from Pauri 13.
